assertions.name: C1_eq98_rank_is_2_not_3
assertions.source: P1 CONFIRMED. det(eq 98) = 0 and its exact rank over Q is 2. The merged probe's C4 said 'eq (98) is a rank-3 antisymmetric integer matrix' -- that is its SIZE, used as a RANK. Every odd-size antisymmetric matrix is singular (det A = det(-A^T) = (-1)^n det A), so an antisymmetric matrix always has EVEN rank and 'rank 3' was never available

assertions.name: C2_the_real_invariant_is_the_elementary_divisor
assertions.source: P2 CONFIRMED. A rank-2 antisymmetric integral form is [[0,d],[-d,0]] (+) 0 up to GL(Z), so the elementary divisor d is the complete invariant. d(eq 98) = 1, d(NZ cusp) = 2: inequivalent over Z. This is the discriminator the merged probe should have used

assertions.name: C3_they_are_Q_equivalent
assertions.source: P3 CONFIRMED. Both forms have rank 2, and over Q a rank-2 antisymmetric form is unique up to equivalence, so they are Q-equivalent and differ only by the integral factor 2. A charge lattice is routinely defined up to normalisation, which is exactly why this is not an exclusion

assertions.name: C4_rescoped_b_to_a_NZ_is_NOT_excluded
assertions.source: The merged C4 was labelled scope-(b), which AGENTS.md reserves for exclusions resting on a PROVED invariant. The invariant cited was a miscomputed rank, so the (b) label was unearned. Re-scoped to (a): the NZ cusp form is not on the nose the eq-(98) form (integral factor 2, and indexed by (mu,lambda) rather than by the three sigma). The NZ route is NOT excluded -- charge lattices are routinely defined up to normalisation and the two forms agree over Q

assertions.name: C5_only_C4_is_void
assertions.source: The merged probe's C1, C2, C3, C5 and C7 are measurements and stand unchanged. Only C4 -- which turned the C2+C3 measurements into an exclusion via the bogus rank comparison -- is void. The defect is in one inference, not in the data

assertions.name: C6_d1_vs_d2_is_normalisation_not_obstruction
assertions.source: The NZ cusp form halves to [[0,1],[-1,0]], which is unimodular, so it is 2 x a unimodular rank-2 form while eq (98) is already unimodular on its support. The elementary divisors differ by an overall factor 2 -- a normalisation convention for the NZ symplectic form, not an obstruction. So even the re-scoped scope-(a) statement ('differs by an integral factor 2') is NOT evidence against the NZ route

assertions.name: C7_the_real_difference_is_the_radical_and_it_is_forced
assertions.source: eq (98) has a 1-dimensional radical spanned by the axis vector (-3, -3, 4), verified by eq(98) . axis = [0,0,0]. This is FORCED: any 3x3 antisymmetric matrix is the cross-product matrix of its axis vector (Omega_23, -Omega_13, Omega_12), so the radical being built from the Omega entries carries no information and must not be read as numerology. After C6 removes the elementary-divisor gap, THIS is the only surviving structural difference from the NZ cusp form: a rank-3 lattice with a 1-dim radical versus a rank-2 lattice with none. In Seiberg-Witten terms a null direction of the Dirac pairing is a FLAVOUR charge, so the open question for the NZ route is not 'why rank 2' but 'where is the third, null direction'

description: qou-rutm. CORRECTS A MERGED CLAIM. d1b_52_charge_lattice_sourcing_probe is on main (74a927b6af, PR #6599) and its headline verdict C4 reads 'eq (98) is a rank-3 antisymmetric integer matrix; the NZ datum's antisymmetric content has rank 2, always; scope-(b) exclusion'. eq (98) has rank 2, not 3: I wrote its SIZE (3x3) and used it as a RANK. This was never possible -- every odd-size antisymmetric matrix is singular (det A = det(-A^T) = (-1)^n det A), so an antisymmetric matrix always has EVEN rank. det(eq 98) = 0, rank = 2 exactly. So the comparison put a size against a rank and BOTH objects are rank 2, which makes the NZ cusp block MORE plausible as a carrier rather than less. The real discriminator is the elementary divisor of a rank-2 antisymmetric integral form, complete up to GL(Z): d(eq 98) = 1 against d(NZ cusp) = 2, so they are inequivalent over Z but EQUIVALENT over Q. Verdict re-scoped (b) -> (a) per AGENTS.md, which reserves (b) for exclusions resting on a proved invariant: the NZ cusp form is not on the nose the eq-(98) form, but THE NZ ROUTE IS NOT EXCLUDED -- charge lattices are routinely defined up to normalisation. The merged C1, C2, C3, C5 and C7 are measurements and stand; only C4 is void.
